name: Birim Private Files – Protect Uploads & Private Pages
author: Melih Birim

sections.description:
WordPress stores uploads in /wp-content/uploads/, and every file there is a public URL. Making a page private, or putting your site behind a login, does not protect the files on it: anyone with the link can open them.

Birim Private Files routes every request for an uploaded file through WordPress and only serves it to people who are allowed to see it.

  • Three ways to decide who opens files: any logged-in user, only the roles you choose, or only the people each file is shared with (the uploader, people you add in the file’s “Shared with” field, editors and administrators).
  • Private pages too: a “Who can view” box in the page editor (block editor and classic editor) sets each page or post to Everyone, Logged-in users or chosen roles. Restricted pages send logged-out visitors to the login page, and their text is hidden in search results, archives, feeds and the REST API, and left out of the sitemap.
  • Files follow their page: in per-file mode, files uploaded to a restricted page open for whoever can view that page.
  • A “My files” list: put [birim_my_files] on a page and each person sees the files they uploaded or that were shared with them.
  • Direct links are protected, not just pages. Logged-out visitors who open a file link are sent to the login page and come back to the file after logging in.
  • It checks that protection really works. After you turn it on, the plugin requests a test file from your site as a logged-out visitor and tells you the result: Protected, Not protected, or Could not check. Until protection is confirmed, administrators see a warning. Many file protection setups fail silently on nginx servers; this one tells you.
  • Apache: rules are added to wp-content/uploads/.htaccess automatically, and removed when you deactivate the plugin.
  • nginx: the settings page shows the exact two-line rule to add for your site.
  • Public exceptions: keep chosen files public, such as a logo, with simple patterns like public/*.
  • Files are served with private caching headers (so CDNs and shared caches do not store them), conditional requests and byte ranges, so video seeking works.
  • Script files are never served from uploads, and paths outside the uploads folder are refused.
  • Lightweight: one file, no tracking, no external requests, no ads.

What you can do with it

  • Staff intranet: share HR policies, handbooks, rotas and internal reports on WordPress. Only staff who log in can open them, even if a link is forwarded outside the company.
  • Client portal: agencies, freelancers, accountants and lawyers share each contract, design or report with one client, who sees it in their “My files” page. Other clients cannot open it, even with the link.
  • Members-only content: sell or share course PDFs, e-books, worksheets and videos without the download link being passed around. Video seeking still works.
  • Schools, clubs and charities: keep photos of children, member lists and meeting minutes visible to parents and members only.
  • Forms that collect documents: CVs, ID scans and signed forms uploaded through form plugins usually land in the public uploads folder. Keep them away from anyone who guesses or finds the link.
  • Staging and pre-launch sites: stop unreleased product images and documents from leaking or showing up in Google Images.

What it does not do

  • Titles of restricted pages can still appear in menus and archive lists; only their text is hidden.
  • WordPress’s public REST API lists media items (titles and links) to anyone. The files themselves stay protected, but to hide the list as well, use a REST API lockdown plugin such as Birim REST Lock.
  • It does not encrypt files on the server or make your site compliant with any regulation on its own. It controls who can open them.

For developers

  • birim_private_files_can_access filter: ( bool $allowed, string $relative_path ) to make your own access decisions, for example per file or per user.
  • birim_private_files_served action: ( string $relative_path, string $absolute_path ), fired just before an allowed file is sent, for example to log downloads.
  • birim_private_files_serve( $path, array( 'download' => true ) ) sends a file as a download (attachment) instead of inline.
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins > Add New, or upload the birim-private-files folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin. Nothing changes until you turn protection on.
  3. Go to Settings > Private Files, tick “Make uploaded files private” and save.
  4. Check the status. On nginx, add the rule shown, reload nginx and click “Check again”.
sections.faq:
Will images on my public pages break?

Yes, for logged-out visitors, unless the files match a public exception. This plugin is meant for sites where the content is private too. Use the public exceptions for files that must stay visible, such as a logo.

The status says “Not protected”.

Your web server is serving files directly without asking WordPress. On nginx, add the rule shown on the settings page. On Apache, your host may not allow .htaccess rewrite rules, or it may run nginx in front of Apache; send your host the rule shown on the settings page.

The status says “Could not check”.

Your server could not make a request to its own website, which some hosts block. Check manually: copy the link of an uploaded file, open a private browser window and paste it. You should see the login page or “This file is private”.

Does it slow down my site?

Each file request now starts WordPress to check the login, so files are served a little slower than directly by the web server. Logged-in browsers cache files for an hour.

I use a CDN.

Files are sent with Cache-Control: private, which CDNs respect by default. If your CDN is set to cache everything regardless of headers, exclude /wp-content/uploads/ from that rule.

What happens when I deactivate the plugin?

On Apache the rules are removed and files are public again. On nginx, remove the rule you added, or file links will stop working.

Does it work on multisite?

Not yet. Multisite support is planned.

How do I report a security issue?

Please email security@birim.one instead of posting in the forum. See https://birimone.pages.dev/security/ for the full policy.

short_description: Protect uploaded files and pages: open only for logged-in users, chosen roles or people you share them with, even by direct link. Checks it works.
